derivation: from H2179 (זָנַב) (in the original sense of flapping);

occurrences.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Put forth thine hand, and take it by the tail. And he put forth his hand, and caught it, and it became a rod in his hand:

And the Lord shall make thee the head, and not the tail; and thou shalt be above only, and thou shalt not be beneath; if that thou hearken unto the commandments of the Lord thy God, which I command thee this day, to observe and to do them:
And Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took firebrands, and turned tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the midst between two tails.
He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.
And say unto him, Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted for the two tails of these smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.
Therefore the Lord will cut off from Israel head and tail, branch and rush, in one day.
Neither shall there be any work for Egypt, which the head or tail, branch or rush, may do.
